clue.text: One piano dropped into mine shaft just for a lark

indicators.note: the two letters are let fall inside the shaft, so they go within its word

parts.note: a pit is a mine or its shaft
the Roman numeral one is I
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: Someone tosses a coin down a mine shaft simply for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just for a lark' reads as 'for fun', but 'lark' is a bird: I and P go inside PIT after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The small songbird of fields is lark-like in look and song, and one kind is even called the titlark.

clue.text: He buys tea to hearten the chief steward

indicators.note: putting something into the heart of a word is a container signal

parts.note: a purser is the officer in charge of a ship's money and stores, its chief steward
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: A man brings tea to cheer up the head steward on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hearten' means to put into the heart; 'He buys' looks like the start of a sentence but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A buyer is a man who acquires goods for payment.

clue.text: One who throws a large jug

explanation.surface: A man who throws a big jug.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball the bowler figure who delivers the ball, and also a big container with a handle and lip for pouring.

clue.text: Gratitude twice expressed in valedictory words

indicators.note: the word is said two times, so its letters appear a second time

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: Thanks said two times in a farewell speech.
explanation.walkthrough: TA, British slang for thanks, written twice gives an informal British farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Valedictory words are said on parting, and this is a childish British way to say goodbye.

clue.text: Pull in a drunkard from the aristocracy

indicators.note: the word for pull is set within the word for a drunkard

parts.note: a toper is a heavy drinker
to draw is to pull

explanation.surface: Bring a drunk in off the street, someone of noble birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'Pull' looks like a verb acting on the drunkard but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the highest social class, a phrase from the best drawer where valuables are kept.

clue.text: Daughter in authority gets contract to produce cosmetic accessory

indicators.note: the single letter goes within the word for authority

parts.note: power means authority or control
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees
a compact is an agreement or contract

explanation.surface: A daughter in a powerful job signs a deal to make make-up gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'gets' and 'to produce' are link words joining the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A small flat case holding face powder and a mirror, carried in a handbag for touching up make-up.

clue.text: In cholera recovery is most unusual

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words cholera recovery, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: A recovery from cholera is a very uncommon event.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seldom found is exceptionally unusual.

clue.text: Facing a terrible defeat, you and I tire

indicators.note: the words for you and I are placed in front of the rest, facing it

parts.note: we means you and I together
a rout is a crushing defeat

explanation.surface: Facing a heavy defeat, we grow weary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facing' tells you the 'you and I' piece stands in front of the defeat; the comma is surface punctuation only.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear out is to exhaust or fatigue someone, a phrasal synonym of tire.

clue.text: Discharge an ambassador stuck into hard liquor

indicators.note: one word is pushed inside the other, a container signal

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a hard liquor
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: An envoy is caught up in strong drink and sent away.
explanation.walkthrough: His Excellency is the formal style of an ambassador, abbreviated in crosswords; 'stuck into' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A watery mucus flowing from the eyes or nose is a bodily discharge.

clue.text: Renegade takes three aback by knocking on the door

parts.note: a rat is a deserter or turncoat

indicators.note: the answer to clue three is taken backwards

parts.note: refers to the solution of 3-down in this puzzle, a farewell

explanation.surface: A deserter takes three steps back as someone raps at the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three' is a cross-reference to the 3-down answer, not a number; 'aback' turns it round before it joins the renegade.
explanation.definitionFit: The word imitates the sound of repeated knocks, an onomatopoeic name for rapping.

clue.text: Kindly offer to attend Sir Edward's lecture

parts.note: to tender is to offer
to attend a talk by Sir Edward (Ted) is to hear Ted, HEAR + TED

explanation.surface: A gracious invitation to go to a talk given by a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted is the short form of Edward, so listening to his lecture is to HEAR TED.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindly as an adjective describes a compassionate, gentle and sympathetic nature.

clue.text: Distortion revealed by a military attendant

parts.note: war is the military business of fighting
a page is a young attendant

explanation.surface: A soldier's servant shows something twisted.
explanation.definitionFit: Twisting out of shape, as wood bends when it dries unevenly.

clue.text: Two men snigger

indicators.note: two of the same pronoun are written side by side

parts.note: he is the pronoun for each man

explanation.surface: A pair of chaps snicker.
explanation.walkthrough: HE stands for a man; 'Two' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: A written suppressed giggle or titter, the sound of a sly laugh.

clue.text: Put in a grave together

explanation.surface: Bury the pair side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To bury a body, and the Latin preposition meaning between or among, used as a prefix for mutual or together.

clue.text: Sound barrier

explanation.surface: The noise of breaking through the barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep resonant roar, and a floating chain or beam stretched across a harbour to block ships.

clue.text: Gaiters worn by an Irishman on board

indicators.note: being on board a ship means being inside the letters for a steamship

parts.note: board suggests a ship, abbreviated SS for steamship
Pat, short for Patrick, is the stock Irishman of crosswords

explanation.surface: Ankle coverings worn by an Irishman on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the convention for inside SS, the steamship: PAT goes within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Short cloth coverings over the shoe and ankle are a kind of gaiter.

clue.text: It was changed in the middle

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: It was altered in the centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' signals an anagram of IT WAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The narrow part of the body between ribs and hips is its midriff or middle.

clue.text: Old metal dealer becomes a boxing promoter

explanation.surface: A dealer in old metal becomes a fight promoter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone trading in waste iron, and humorously a merchant of fights, since a scrap is a brawl.

clue.text: Precipitous headland on the Medway estuary

parts.note: sheer means very steep
a ness is a promontory, as in many coastal place names

explanation.surface: A steep promontory where the Medway meets the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The town is a port in Kent, at the mouth of the River Medway in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kent port stands on the Isle of Sheppey at the Medway mouth.

clue.text: Understood the answering machine was working

explanation.surface: Grasped that the answerphone was functioning.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for comprehended, and literally a recorded voice note received.

clue.text: Age ill-disposed to old supporter of Copernicus

indicators.note: the letters are arranged afresh, disposed in another order

explanation.surface: An era hostile to an early ally of Copernicus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-disposed' hides the split: 'ill' is fodder with 'Age', and 'disposed' is the anagram signal; O follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian astronomer championed the sun-centred model of the heavens and was tried for it.

clue.text: A pair of pages needing relaxation and calm

parts.note: p is the abbreviation for page, so two pages are PP
ease is rest or relaxation

explanation.surface: Two pages need rest and quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: To pacify or soothe someone, making them quiet.

clue.text: Be inclined to use a lance

explanation.surface: Be minded to use a lance.
explanation.definitionFit: To lean or slope, and to joust with a lance in a medieval contest.

clue.text: Make sure the water bowl is full for a young dog

definitions.text: Make sure the water bowl is full

parts.note: to can mean for, as in a present to someone
a pup is a young dog

explanation.surface: Keep the water dish filled for the puppy.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition of the phrase; the last three words also split it as a two-word wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Refilling to the brim, the action described for the bowl.

clue.text: Tales which can be taken either way

indicators.text: which can be taken either way
indicators.note: the word reads the same from either end, so it is a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Stories that may be interpreted in two ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken either way' looks like ambiguity but means the word reads identically backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Long heroic stories, originally Norse and Icelandic prose narratives.

clue.text: After spring run and box

indicators.note: the letter for run comes after the word for spring

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: After a spring jog, a boxing session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places R after SPA; to spar is to practise boxing.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to fight with the fists in practice.

clue.text: Word in French and English for a speck of dust

parts.note: mot is French for word

explanation.surface: A term in French and English for a fleck of dust.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny particle, as in the biblical speck in a brother's eye.

clue.text: Bob gets a short, sharp smack

explanation.surface: Bob gets a quick slap.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut short like a bobbed haircut, and a quick blow such as a cuff round the ear.

clue.text: Leave and move into the fast lane

explanation.surface: Depart and swing into the outside lane.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw or depart, and to steer out from behind a vehicle to overtake.

clue.text: Working the land right up to retirement

parts.note: till means up to a given time
retirement age, the point of retiring, gives age

explanation.surface: Farming continued right until one retires.
explanation.definitionFit: Ploughing and cultivation of soil for crops.

clue.text: Supporting one who sells animal food

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a vender, variant of vendor, is a seller

explanation.surface: Backing a seller of animal feed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry fodder for livestock, or more broadly provisions.

clue.text: Put the squeeze on Fleet Street

explanation.surface: Pressure Fleet Street.
explanation.definitionFit: To push or urge hard, and the newspaper trade, long based in that London street.
